title: Neuro-Symbolic Agentic AI for Networked Low-Altitude UAVs
neural_component: Neural modules interpret multimodal observations, mission instructions, and contextual inputs to ground objects, states, and reusable skills.
symbolic_component: Task/goal management, symbolic rules and skill preconditions, neuro-symbolic planning, verification/metacognition, shared knowledge/memory, and explicit evidence conditions.
coupling_mechanism: Neural grounding feeds an agentic symbolic planning and verification loop; execution/connectivity feedback updates task state and triggers sensing or replanning.
inclusion_rationale: Candidate direct UAV position paper: full-text review confirms a reference NSAAI architecture and an illustrative LAESim urban fire-inspection case, but not a standalone evaluated algorithm. It should not be counted as a core method.
summary: Full-text review: presents an NSAAI reference architecture (task/goal management, neuro-symbolic planning, verification/metacognition, skill execution/network interaction, shared knowledge/memory) and an illustrative LAESim urban fire-inspection case with evidence-grounded skill reuse.
limitations: Position/architecture article rather than a benchmarked method. The available full text describes the use case qualitatively; no independent quantitative benchmark table, hardware-in-the-loop study, or real-flight validation was identified in the reviewed HTML version.
evidence_legacy: Full-text HTML version at https://arxiv.org/html/2609.19961v1 was read on 2026-09-20; it presents a reference architecture and an illustrative LAESim use case rather than a standalone benchmarked method.

evidence_items.claim: The full text presents a reference architecture and an illustrative LAESim urban fire-inspection case, rather than a standalone quantitative method evaluation.

title: NEUROSYMLAND: Neuro-Symbolic Landing-Site Assessment for Robust and Edge-Deployable UAV Autonomy
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering, Vol. 3, FSE, Article FSE146, July 2026
neural_component: An INT8-quantized SegFormer-B0 with geometric post-processing constructs a probabilistic semantic scene graph (PSSG) from onboard visual input.
symbolic_component: Deterministic Scallop rules express terrain-flatness, obstacle-clearance, and spatial-consistency constraints over the PSSG. Rules are authored offline with LLM assistance and refined with a human in the loop.
coupling_mechanism: Neural perception populates the PSSG; deterministic symbolic rules then evaluate candidate landing regions over that explicit representation. The runtime does not query the LLM; LLM-assisted authoring occurs offline before deployment.
inclusion_rationale: Candidate direct UAV work: neural perception and explicit symbolic safety reasoning are functionally coupled for landing-site assessment. Full-text review and venue conflict resolution are required before inclusion.
summary: NeuroSymLand combines an INT8-quantized SegFormer-B0 with geometric post-processing into a probabilistic semantic scene graph (PSSG), then executes deterministic Scallop safety rules for landing-site assessment. The full text reports 61 successful assessments out of 72 simulated scenarios, 100 hardware-in-the-loop profiling trials, and edge-resource profiling. Code is available at https://github.com/Janus117/NeuroSymbolicLand. Rules are authored offline with LLM assistance and refined with a human in the loop; runtime execution does not query the LLM.
limitations: Full-text review found no real-flight validation; reported evidence is simulation and hardware-in-the-loop. Venue metadata is unresolved (arXiv comments say IROS 2026 while the journal reference says Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering, Vol. 3, FSE, Article FSE146), and the DOI has not been confirmed against a publisher record. The runtime symbolic engine is deterministic, but rule authoring depends on an offline LLM-assisted and human-in-the-loop workflow.

title: NEUSIS: A Compositional Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Autonomous Perception, Reasoning, and Planning in Complex UAV Search Missions
neural_component: GRiD integrates vision foundation models, a fine-tuned CLIP classifier for object attributes/types, 2D tracking, and LLM-generated reasoner code adapted from HYDRA to ground objects in 3D from RGB, depth, and GPS.
symbolic_component: A probabilistic world model accumulates noisy GRiD detections with Bayesian position filtering, discrete attribute ranking, physical constraints, and explicit reporting; SNaC performs hierarchical selection, navigation, and coverage planning.
coupling_mechanism: GRiD neural perception produces noisy symbolic detections and attributes; the probabilistic world model reasons over and accumulates those symbols, then SNaC consumes the updated belief map for hierarchical planning.
inclusion_rationale: Meets the four scope criteria after source-based review of the neural component, explicit symbolic mechanism, functional coupling and described UAV validation. Inclusion is a review decision, not human review or independent replication.
summary: GRiD neural perception and generated programs feed a persistent probabilistic world model; MiniZinc AOI selection and hierarchical navigation guide search. AirSim/HAMERITT comparisons and component ablations are reported.
limitations: Simulation only. The world model starts with ground-truth occupancy/BEV maps and relies on accurate localization/depth. Table I SR measures entity localization within 5 m, not whole-mission success or flight safety; false positives require separate F1/precision analysis.
classification_rationale: Primary theme is perception and world modeling because GRiD grounding and the probabilistic world model are the central coupling; SNaC planning and navigation are secondary.
evidence_legacy: Full-text HTML version was read on 2026-09-20; GRiD, the probabilistic world model, SNaC, and HAMERITT/AirSim evaluation were verified. Official GitHub repository was located by web search.

title: LLM-Enabled Low-Altitude UAV Natural Language Navigation via Signal Temporal Logic Specification Translation and Repair
neural_component: Qwen2.5-0.5B translator adapted using LoRA/SFT and GRPO; an LLM selects repair dimensions.
symbolic_component: STL formulas, mixed-integer trajectory constraints, IIS conflict diagnosis and protected safety predicates.
coupling_mechanism: The LLM proposes STL; solver conflicts guide temporal/predicate repair while the optimization layer chooses relaxation magnitudes.
inclusion_rationale: Meets the four scope criteria after source-based review of the neural component, explicit symbolic mechanism, functional coupling and described UAV validation. Inclusion is a review decision, not human review or independent replication.
summary: Links language translation, constrained trajectory synthesis and specification repair. Table I reports 98% normalized formula exact match; a separate outdoor DJI Matrice 300 RTK demonstration is described.
limitations: Known geometry and simplified dynamics; translation/planning run offboard. Formula exact match is not semantic equivalence or a flight-safety rate. The outdoor example does not establish broad operational robustness; formal encoding and repair assumptions require independent audit.
classification_rationale: Abstract-level classification: NL-to-STL translation and MILP trajectory synthesis place the work primarily in navigation and control; reasoning and safety are secondary.

title: Reasoning Knowledge-Gap in Drone Planning via LLM-based Active Elicitation
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Symposium Series 8(1), 127-131 (2026)
neural_component: A vision-language model processes RGB-D observations and constructs a local semantic map; an LLM selects optimal binary questions for active human elicitation.
symbolic_component: The Minimal Information Neuro-Symbolic Tree (MINT) explicitly structures obstacle and goal knowledge gaps; a hierarchical planner evaluates trajectory cost/divergence and goal entropy over hypothesis branches.
coupling_mechanism: The VLM identifies semantic uncertainty; MINT represents it as a symbolic tree; the LLM chooses a binary query; the human answer prunes the tree and updates the semantic map and plan.
inclusion_rationale: Meets the four scope criteria after source-based review of the neural component, explicit symbolic mechanism, functional coupling and described UAV validation. Inclusion is a review decision, not human review or independent replication.
summary: MINT structures knowledge gaps about obstacles and goals into a queryable neuro-symbolic tree, uses an LLM to ask optimal binary questions, and updates plans after human responses. It integrates VLM perception, voice interaction, and low-level UAV control in NVIDIA Isaac simulations and real-world quadrotor trials.
limitations: Simulation success/query counts and a separate 20-trial physical demonstration are small, task-specific results. Human answers are treated as reliable; model details, query optimality and failure coverage need further validation. This is an AAAI Spring Symposium paper, not an AAAI main-conference paper.
classification_rationale: Primary theme is collaboration and interaction because active human-UAV knowledge elicitation is the central contribution; MINT reasoning also supports mission planning as a secondary theme.
evidence_legacy: Full-text HTML version was read on 2026-09-20; MINT, NVIDIA Isaac simulation, and real-world quadrotor deployment were verified.

title: TypeFly: Flying Drones with Large Language Model
neural_component: GPT-4 generates plans and answers runtime queries; YOLOv8 provides scene descriptions.
symbolic_component: MiniSpec programs with explicit conditionals, bounded loops, skill calls and exception handling.
coupling_mechanism: Neural outputs become executable programs; the interpreter invokes skills and requests replanning using updated observations.
inclusion_rationale: Included under the explicit-program branch of this proposed taxonomy, not merely because it uses an LLM. MiniSpec control flow and runtime interpretation couple neural generation to real UAV execution.
summary: Indoor Tello experiments evaluate 11 tasks with 10 repetitions each. MiniSpec and streaming interpretation reduce command-to-first-action delay in the reported setup.
limitations: Program restrictions are not a collision-safety proof. Task 9 succeeds in 7/10 trials, exposing geometric reasoning failures. Results depend on an edge server, remote LLM and a small indoor task set.
